Hi all — answering Sophie directly below and attaching the artifacts. I kept the wording conservative for legal review; happy to iterate.

From: Sophie Müller (questions summarized)

1) SOC 2 Type II report and audit period
- Attached: SOC2_Type_II_Redwood_2024-2025.pdf (attestation). Audit period covered: 2024-05-01 to 2025-04-30.
- Report includes trust services criteria relevant to security and availability. Pricing/usage telemetry is not included in the report scope.

2) Bridge letter
- We can provide a signed bridge letter that confirms no materially adverse control changes since the report end date and reconfirms controls coverage through the bridge period. Draft attached: redwood_bridge_letter_draft.pdf.
- Suggested language covers data residency assertions for hosted customers and points to contractual commitments. Legal prefers to review any customer-specific language; we typically sign a bridge for procurement purposes.

3) Hosting boundary (hosted/shared offering)
- Data at rest (customer content) for EU-region customers is stored in EU cloud regions (currently eu-west-1 and eu-west-2) and encrypted at rest.
- Control plane (management APIs, orchestration) is provisioned in a segregated service layer. For the standard hosted offering, some control-plane telemetry (lower fidelity operational metrics) may be aggregated in Redwood's central control plane which currently has presence outside the EU.
- Importantly: customer unencrypted content does not leave the EU for inference by default for EU-configured model endpoints. Any cross-border processing is governed by contract terms and explicit routing policies.

4) EU-only residency options
- Dedicated (reserved capacity in EU regions) — same SLA as hosted; can be provisioned within ~4–6 weeks depending on capacity. Dedicated ensures compute and storage remain in-region and isolates customer workload.
- Private deployment (VPC / on-prem) — available for customers requiring maximum isolation; timeline and SLAs vary (typically 8–12 weeks for on-prem, faster for VPC with our partners).

5) KMS / BYOK
- Hosted: we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed envelope keys for certain enterprise customers via an EU KMS (subject to contractual setup). For standard hosted customers, Redwood-managed KMS is used (keys stored in EU region when EU tenancy is requested).
- Dedicated & Private: full BYOK/CMK support (customer-provided KMS/HSM integrations).

Next steps I recommend:
- Jasmine, confirm RheinBank's expected contract start date so we can tailor the bridge period wording.
- Sophie/Lisa: please review the attached draft bridge letter and the SOC 2 PDF. We'll upload CAIQ answers to the shared drive; link included below.

Notes on artifacts attached: SOC2 PDF (redacted where necessary), draft bridge letter, and a working CAIQ/response workbook. If RheinBank prefers sealed attestation copies via NDA or secure transfer, we can accommodate.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2_Type_II_Redwood_2024-2025.pdf; redwood_bridge_letter_draft.pdf; redwood_ca iq_responses.xlsx
